n: A heartfelt testimony: ‘I love the LORD, because he heard me.’ Answered prayer deepens love for God.
Because God bent down to listen, the psalmist will keep praying all his life.
Death’s ropes wrapped around him and the terrors of the grave seized him. He was in deep trouble and grief.

f.g: Literally ‘the cords of death,’ like ropes.
Hebrew Sheol, the grave or realm of the dead.

n: He cried out in a short, urgent prayer: ‘O LORD, save my life!’

f.w: Then called I upon the name of the LORD

n: God is gracious, righteous, and merciful — kindness and justice together.
The Lord protects the ‘simple’ — the humble and unsophisticated who rely on him.

f.g: The naive or unprotected; those who can’t defend themselves.

n: He tells his soul to return to calm rest, because God has been so generous.

f.w: Return unto thy rest, O my soul

n: God rescued his life from death, his eyes from tears, and his feet from stumbling.
Restored to life, he will live in God’s presence among the living.
He kept believing even when severely afflicted, and spoke because he believed. Paul quotes this as a model of faith-filled testimony.

f.w: I believed, therefore have I spoken

n: In panic he had concluded that no human could be relied on — only God proved trustworthy.
‘How can I ever repay the Lord?’ — the natural question of a grateful heart.
He will lift a cup of thanksgiving, perhaps a drink offering at the temple, and call on God’s name. Jews drink cups of blessing at Passover; Latter-day Saints may think of the sacramental cup.
He will fulfill the vows he made while in trouble, publicly before God’s people.
The death of God’s faithful ones is ‘precious’ — costly, weighty — to him. He does not take it lightly; each life matters, and he cares for his saints in life and death.

f.g: Costly, of great worth, not lightly permitted.

n: He declares himself God’s servant, born into his service like the son of a servant woman. God has untied the ropes of death that bound him.

f.g: Born a servant in God’s household — belonging to him from birth.

n: He will offer a thanksgiving sacrifice and call on the Lord.
He repeats his vow for emphasis: he will keep his promises publicly.

f.w: in the presence of all his people

n: The setting is the temple courts in Jerusalem. The psalm ends with ‘Hallelujah.’

f.w: the courts of the LORD's house
